walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term ostranenie (defamiliarisation) in 1917?
options: Viktor Shklovsky
Roman Jakobson
Boris Eikhenbaum
Yuri Tynyanov

mcqs.q: Whose 1946 essay attacked the intentional fallacy?
options: Wimsatt and Beardsley
Brooks and Warren
Frye and Bloom
Empson and Richards

mcqs.q: Why distinguish the speaker of a poem from the poet?
options: Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.
The speaker of a poem is always the poet themselves.
The speaker is the voice constructed in the poem; the poet is the writer. Treating them as identical can mislead, especially with dramatic monologues or personae.

mcqs.q: Why are genre conventions important when interpreting a text?
options: Genre is just a label to help bookshops categorise novels.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
They set reader expectations the text can fulfil or subvert; analysing how a text uses or breaks conventions reveals its meaning and significance.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
